Jordan (CS): Hey team — Raptor AI just sent a request to get a domain-tuned 13B model into production. They want private deployment or dedicated capacity, PHI filtering, and HSM keying. Putting the intake here so we can triage.
Maya (Solutions): Quick q — are they bringing model artifacts or asking us to pick an open variant? :thinking_face:
Jordan (CS): They uploaded artifacts to a secure bucket and included a short spec. It's proprietary fine-tuned weights + tokenizer. Link shared in ticket. They also called out a renewal discussion in 90 days (they're budget-sensitive).
Ken (Eng): Ok. First engineering check: model architecture + tokenizer format. Also need to know if it's already quantized. If not, we'll test int8/fp16 tradeoffs.
Jordan (CS): Uploaded: s3://redwood-cs/raptor/13b-v2.tar.gz (internal link in ticket).
Ava (Security): Heads up — training data includes customer support transcripts, likely PHI. We need privacy scan + data retention rules. They explicitly requested no logging to external buckets.
Ken (Eng): We support route-level no-persist. Example config we can apply on staging:
```route: "/raptor/v1"
persist_kv_cache: false
log_to_s3: false
kms: "customer-hsm"
```
Maya (Solutions): For acceptance/evals I propose: latency smoke (p95 < 1.2s), quality baseline on ~200 example prompts (ROUGE/EM), and a safety stress suite with 1k prompts targeting PHI/PII leakage. I can assemble the prompt set.
Sam (CSM): FYI Raptor is marked as a renewal risk if we don't get a pilot live before their renewal window. They've indicated willingness to pay for Dedicated if it speeds time-to-live.
Jordan (CS): Decision fork: Dedicated pool to start vs Private (VPC + on-prem connector). Which is faster?
Ken (Eng): Dedicated is faster — we can allocate 2x A10G nodes and run compatibility tests within 48 hours. Private requires infra onboarding and HSM key exchange — estimate ~2 weeks.
Ava (Security): For Private we need customer HSM inventory + key policy, signed DPA, and compliance signoff. No-go without those. Also request: prove we can enforce no-persist at the runtime and disable telemetry.
Maya (Solutions): I'll draft an eval matrix and a short runbook for the pilot (endpoint config, rollback policy, canary %, monitoring). Will include prompts for quality checks and an A/B quality pass threshold.
Jordan (CS): Can Engineering and Security ack we can meet the security requirements (no-logs, HSM) on Dedicated as a short-term compromise?
Ken (Eng): We can support HSM-backed keys on Dedicated and enforce runtime no-persist flags. Need a copy of the model tokenizer and a small sample of tokens to sanity-check tokenization.
Ava (Security): Short-term: ok to proceed with Dedicated with the HSM config and strict no-persist policy, but Security must run a full assessment before Private.
Maya (Solutions): I'll schedule a short enablement/demo for the customer once the pilot endpoint is up. Suggested checklist: 1) smoke perf tests 2) safety stress 3) ops runbook 4) contract extension options documented.
Jordan (CS): Great. @Ken @Ava @Maya please ack and I'll book a 30-min sync with Raptor for tomorrow 10:00am PT to confirm scope.
Ken (Eng): Ack.
Ava (Security): Ack.
Maya (Solutions): Ack :thumbsup:
orion-bot: Meeting created: "Raptor model intake: kickoff" — tomorrow 10:00am PT. Invite sent to participants.
Jordan (CS): Added acceptance criteria to ticket CS-4821: security signoff, eval pass (quality + safety), deploy plan, renewal negotiation flagged to Sales/CSM.
Sam (CSM): Will start concurrent renewal conversation and capture extension options in the ticket.
Jordan (CS): Thanks everyone — I'll update the ticket with the direct artifact link and meeting notes post-sync. Follow-ups will live in CS-4821.
